title: Product Governance and Fair Value
summary: How to assess firms' product design, target market definition, testing, fair value assessments and post-sale review across the product lifecycle.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to assess firms' product design, target market definition, testing, fair value assessments and post-sale review across the product lifecycle.
Learning Objectives: Assess product approval, target market and distribution strategy
Apply a fair value framework to a financial product
Evaluate post-sale monitoring and product review
Syllabus: The product lifecycle: design, approval, distribution and review
Target market definition and consumer testing
Fair value: price, quality, cross-subsidy and outcomes
Post-sale monitoring and product withdrawal or remediation
Intended Audience: Conduct and consumer protection supervisors, including those supervising retail-facing firms
Prudential and governance supervisors seeking to assess culture and its link to risk
Policy, data and enforcement staff working on conduct risk and customer outcomes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of conduct or consumer protection supervision is helpful. No background in economics or behavioural science is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
